title: “Double Awareness in Everyday Hospital Life – How Do Internal Medicine Physicians Experience and Deal with ‘Double Awareness’ in Patients with a Poor Prognosis?” A Qualitative Interview Study
summary:
Background
Thanks to advances in medicine, many people with serious, life-limiting illnesses—such as cancer—can lead relatively stable lives over an extended period despite a reduced life expectancy. In doing so, they often experience a tension: on the one hand, they are aware of the finiteness of their lives; on the other hand, they retain hope for a fulfilling life. This phenomenon is referred to as 'double awareness' the simultaneous perception of hope and the approaching end of life.
While this duality is considered beneficial to patients’ health, many doctors and nurses in general palliative care feel overwhelmed by it. Often, talking simultaneously about life goals and wishes for death is mistakenly interpreted as indecision or psychological instability, even though it is precisely an expression of a deep inner struggle. The medical system, which demands clear decisions, frequently fails to recognize this ambivalence.

Research Question
To date, the experience of 'double awareness' has been studied primarily in patients and their relatives. Little is known about how healthcare professionals in general palliative care deal with this double awareness. The research question of the study is therefore:
How do internal medicine physicians experience and deal with the coexistence of finitude and hope ('double awareness') in patients with a poor prognosis?

Methodology  
Study design: Qualitative interview study at the University Hospitals of Würzburg and Freiburg.  
Participants: 5–15 physicians per site (total ≈ 10–30); the aim is to obtain a broad picture by including individuals of different ages, genders, levels of professional experience, and varying attitudes toward the topic of 'double awareness'. 
Data collection: Structured interviews that combine fixed topics (e.g., dealing with hope and letting go) with an open-ended conversation format.  
Analysis: The recordings will be transcribed in full. This will be followed by a qualitative content analysis to identify recurring patterns, attitudes, and response strategies among the medical staff.
conditions: An Exploration of the Phenomenon of 'Double Awareness' in Patients with a Poor Prognosis from the Perspective of Internal Medicine Physicians

interventions.name: Conduction of semi-structured interviews with internal medicine physicians regarding their experiences with the phenomenon of 'double awareness' in patients with a poor prognosis

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Physicians specializing in internal medicine
- At least 1 year of clinical experience in an inpatient setting
- Regular contact with seriously ill or dying patients
- Willingness and ability to discuss one’s own emotional and existential experiences
- Consent form
Exclusion criteria:
- Physicians who do not have contact with critically ill patients
- Physicians experiencing acute personal crises (e.g., burnout, recent bereavement, acute psychological stress)
- Individuals without sufficient German language skills
